heading: 4.5 `unit formula`
text:
### 4.5 `unit formula` [LUNI.4.5]

Cross-dimension named conversions, declared as a pair — one formula in each
direction. Each formula is called at the call site by default; an `implicit` pair additionally
auto-applies at an assignment boundary ([LUNI.4.5.1]).

A formula's expression may use the transcendental functions and `**` with any
exponent, each correctly rounded ([LEXP.3.9.2]), and is evaluated as it is
written, one rounded operation at a time ([LDET.3.4.4]). Every call in it is to a
built-in ([LGRA.9.8.11]).

```
unit_formula     ::= 'unit' 'formula' NAME formula_modifier* ':' NEWLINE
                     INDENT
                         formula_line+
                     DEDENT

formula_modifier ::= 'inverting' | 'implicit'
formula_line     ::= NAME '(' NAME ':' TYPE_SYM ')' ':' TYPE_SYM '=' expression NEWLINE
```

The body holds exactly two formulas, each converting in the opposite direction
to the other; the compiler must reject a body with any other count
(`DS_VALIDATE_UNIT_FORMULA_PAIR_ARITY`).

Each formula's parameter type and return type name a unit symbol or an alias of
one, declared in the file or imported. A dimension is not a unit symbol. The
compiler must reject any other name (`DS_VALIDATE_UNIT_UNKNOWN_SYMBOL`).

#### Modifiers

The modifiers may be written in either order; each appears at most once.

- **`implicit`**: compiler auto-applies at an assignment boundary
  ([LUNI.4.5.1]) when the source and target dimension pair is unambiguous
  (exactly one implicit formula for that pair). Ordering-preserving.
- **`inverting`**: the function is monotone decreasing — larger input yields
  smaller output. At variable-to-variable comparisons the compiler flips the
  comparison operator. Can be combined with `implicit`.
- **`inverting implicit`**: auto-applied at assignment, operator-flipping at
  comparisons.
